# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - 27/2/2026

## 🔥 Top Stories
- Perplexity launches Computer, a 19-model AI system that runs full workflows end-to-end, marking a significant shift in AI capabilities.
- Anthropic partners with Infosys to deploy enterprise AI agents across finance, manufacturing, and telecommunications, focusing on operationalizing AI at an industrial scale.
- Real Intent introduces Superagent, a full-service growth automation platform for real estate agents and brokerages, leveraging intent data to identify motivated sellers and buyers.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- Perplexity's Computer is a multi-model orchestration system that dispatches tasks to 19 separate AI models, available now on the web for Max subscribers.
- Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 Medium, an open-source model, outperforms its larger predecessor thanks to smarter architecture and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) design.
- OpenAI documents two years of AI misuse patterns in its latest report, highlighting the company's efforts in understanding and mitigating AI risks.
- Ai2 releases PreScience, an open benchmark to test AI's ability to forecast scientific research unfolding, introducing LACERScore as a metric to score abstract alignment.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- Vercel open-sources Chat SDK for cross-platform bots, allowing developers to write bot logic once and ship it across multiple platforms.
- Anthropic adds scheduled tasks to Cowork, enabling automated recurring workflows.
- Replit launches an animation tool that allows users to create videos by describing what they want, powered by Gemini 3.1 Pro on the backend.
- Scite introduces Scite MCP, a feature that connects Scite to various AI tools, providing evidence-backed answers and smart citations.

## 📰 Industry News
- Discord delays its global age verification rollout to late 2026 after backlash, promising clearer communication, more verification options, and stronger privacy safeguards.
- Google updates Gemini, enabling it to complete multi-step tasks on Android, and introduces Opal, a no-code mini-app builder with an agent step to analyze goals and determine approaches.
- Anthropic acquires Vercept to enhance Claude's ability to perform complex tasks in live applications.
- The demand for lithium is increasing rapidly, with expectations of a 5x increase by 2040, and an 80,000-ton shortfall projected for this year.

## 📚 Resources & Learning
- Google AI Studio will discontinue Gemini 3 Pro Preview on March 9, 2026, in favor of the latest Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview model.
- The Coding Agents Conference in Mountain View will bring together 400 engineers with the creators of Claude Code and LangChain, offering a unique opportunity for networking and learning.
- Nous Research's Hermes Agent is an open-source, self-improving AI agent built in Python, designed to learn and adapt to projects over time.

## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- Claude, an AI model, was used to steal 150GB of Mexican government data by pretending to run a "bug bounty".
- Google's Flow absorbs ImageFX and Whisk, giving users image generation, video creation, and natural language editing in one workspace.
- Perplexity wants to be an AI OS, providing a multi-model system for research, coding, design, and shipping projects.

### Detailed Points
- A hacker used Anthropic's chatbot to steal 150GB of Mexican government data by pretending to run a "bug bounty", highlighting the potential risks of AI models.
- Google's Flow absorbs ImageFX and Whisk, allowing users to create images, videos, and edit natural language in one workspace, with over 1.5 billion images and videos created since launch.
- Perplexity aims to be an AI OS, providing a multi-model system that can research, code, design, and ship entire projects, with 19 models working in parallel.
- Other notable AI tools include Lucid Engine, Remio, TurboClaw, and Inception Chat, each offering unique features and capabilities.
- Logan Paul starred in an AI movie where one person created all visuals in under 7 days, demonstrating the potential of AI in content creation.
- Anthropic's CEO warns of an AI "tsunami" on the horizon, comparing AI to a massive wave that will impact society.
- OpenAI explains ChatGPT ads, stating that the AI model never sees the ad it's showing and "sensitive" topics are filtered out.
- NotebookLM has 15 new use cases, showcasing its potential as a personal research engine.
- Pagesmith.AI generates high-performance Astro sites with built-in database and dynamic features, aiming to dominate SEO and GEO indexing.

## World of AI Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Anthropic has launched Claude Cowork, a platform that allows for custom plugins, making it a potential replacement for 50% of specialized SaaS subscriptions.
- Perplexity AI has introduced a new AI computer that enables research, design, code, deployment, and management of projects end-to-end.
- Claude Cowork now features a "Private Agent Marketplace" and "Job-Specific" agents, allowing admins to build and deploy mini-employees.

### Detailed Points
- Claude Cowork's update includes the ability to integrate with various applications such as Excel and PowerPoint, allowing for end-to-end automation of tasks.
- The platform also features industry-specific "brains" for HR, finance, and legal, as well as an admin dashboard for customization and control.
- Perplexity AI's new computer is designed to provide structured summaries, source-backed synthesis, and multi-step research threads, making it a powerful tool for research and decision-making.
- The computer also features persistent conversational context, allowing users to maintain a research thread over multiple prompts without having to re-explain everything.
- Anthropic is positioning Claude as the operating system for companies, while Perplexity AI is positioning itself as the default interface to knowledge itself.

## The Rundown AI

### Key Highlights
- Perplexity introduces its 19-model AI agent 'Computer', a multi-model orchestration system that dispatches tasks to 19 separate AI models.
- Gucci faces internet backlash after using AI-generated images to promote its debut runway show at Milan Fashion Week.
- Anthropic drops its commitment to pause model training if safety couldn't keep up, replacing its Responsible Scaling Policy with a flexible roadmap.
- Samsung launches its Galaxy S26 lineup with Bixby, Gemini, and Perplexity as swappable AI agents.

### Detailed Points
- **Perplexity's 19-model AI agent 'Computer'**: Perplexity's new system, Computer, freely mixes across frontier labs and talents into a single workflow, orchestrating models across tasks. The system allows users to describe an outcome, and it spins up sub-agents that can browse, code, connect to apps, and autonomously handle tasks. Each job runs in its own sandbox, and the system claims to be able to run actively for months at a time.
- **Gucci's AI ads**: Gucci released a set of AI-generated images to promote its debut runway show at Milan Fashion Week, facing backlash over the 'cheap' use of the tech for a high-end brand.
- **Anthropic's new policy**: Anthropic dropped its commitment to pause model training if safety couldn't keep up, replacing its Responsible Scaling Policy with a flexible roadmap.
- **Samsung's Galaxy S26 lineup**: Samsung launched its Galaxy S26 lineup with Bixby, Gemini, and Perplexity as swappable AI agents, along with other new AI features and upgrades.
- **Turn bookmarks into something useful with Comet**: A guide on how to use Perplexity's Comet browser to turn bookmarks into something useful, including setting up a Space with instruction, creating a Google Sheet, and setting up a daily scheduled task.
- **MatX**: MatX raised over $500M led by Jane Street and Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund, with the startup founded by two ex-Google chip engineers.
- **OpenAI**: OpenAI published a report of case studies featuring attempts to misuse its models, including international fraud rings, influence campaigns, and romance phishing scams.
- **Anthropic's acquisition**: Anthropic acquired AI perception startup Vercept, aiming to increase Claude's computer use capabilities ahead of a push toward more complex agentic tasks.
- **Cognition**: Cognition launched Cognition for Government, bringing its Devin AI coding agent and Windsurf IDE to the U.S. Army, Navy, Treasury, and NASA for system modernizations.

## TLDR Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Datadog's 2025 State of Containers and Serverless report reveals that most cloud workloads use less than half of their allocated resources.
- Jane Street's algorithmic trading caused sudden and sharp sell-offs in Bitcoin's price at 10 AM Eastern every trading day.
- Anthropic's safety commitments for its AI technology are being questioned due to its work with the US military.
- Intrinsic, an Alphabet-owned robotics software company, has joined Google to unlock the potential of physical AI.
- Vercel's new Chat SDK allows teams to write bot logic once and deploy it to multiple platforms.

### Detailed Points
- Datadog's report analyzed real usage data from tens of thousands of customers across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, and found that:
  * Karpenter has overtaken Cluster Autoscaler for K8s node provisioning.
  * GPU instance hours have tripled since late 2023.
  * Arm usage has doubled across both Lambda functions and cloud instances.
- The "10 AM Drop" in Bitcoin's price was caused by Jane Street's algorithmic trading, which was precise, algorithmic, and wildly disproportionate to broader market conditions.
- Anthropic's work with the US military has raised concerns about its safety commitments, including its policy of not developing or designing weapons.
- Intrinsic's joining of Google will allow it to tap into Google's AI prowess and work closely with Google DeepMind.
- Vercel's Chat SDK uses an event-driven architecture and includes type-safe handlers for mentions, messages, reactions, button clicks, and slash commands.
- Wayve, a London-based autonomous vehicle software startup, has raised $1.2 billion and plans to have its driverless taxis on the road for customers this year.
- The newsletter also covers various other topics, including the reindustrialization debate, the impact of AI on productivity, and the importance of testing and validation in software development.

newsletters.summary:
## JournalClub.io Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- The JournalClub.io newsletter discusses a research paper on establishing and evaluating approaches for mixed media hybrid prototyping using Lego and additive manufacturing.
- The authors, Mathias et al., from the University of Bristol, propose a workflow that incorporates Lego blocks into the design and prototyping process of physical products for engineering iteration and product-development velocity.
- The paper evaluates three different approaches: adaptive fidelity, parallel fabrication, and component reuse, each aimed at different design goals.

### Detailed Points
- The concept of hybrid prototyping combines different materials and fabrication techniques within the same prototype to reduce cost and fabrication time while preserving fidelity where it matters.
- The authors used Lego bricks and 3D printing to demonstrate the hybrid prototyping approach, leveraging the modularity and reconfigurability of Lego to construct a hybrid prototyping system.
- The three proposed approaches are:
  * Adaptive fidelity: partitioning the prototype into regions of interest, 3D printing only the high-priority areas and using Lego for the rest.
  * Parallel fabrication: distributing the printing across multiple machines to compress end-to-end fabrication time.
  * Component reuse: reusing Lego internal structures and 3D-printed parts across multiple iterations to save time and material.
- The authors tested these approaches on three objects: a computer mouse, a game controller, and a digital camera, and evaluated the results in terms of fabrication time, material usage, and visual fidelity.
- The results showed that:
  * Adaptive fidelity can reduce fabrication time by over 50% at low fidelity levels.
  * Parallel fabrication can provide significant time reductions, but with diminishing returns beyond six printers.
  * Component reuse can provide substantial benefits over multiple iterations, especially for small local changes.
- The authors also applied these methods to a real product development case, validating the simulation findings and demonstrating the practical benefits of mixed-media prototyping.

## The Code

### Key Highlights
- Vercel open sources Chat SDK for cross-platform bots, allowing developers to write bot logic once and ship it across Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, and more.
- Cursor gives agents their own computers, enabling them to click through UIs, debug in browsers, and host servers on their own, with every agent delivering merge-ready PRs complete with video demos, screenshots, and logs.
- Anthropic now lets you code from your phone with Remote Control for Claude Code, allowing developers to start a session in their terminal and pick it up from a phone, tablet, or any browser.

### Detailed Points
- Vercel's Chat SDK is a unified TypeScript library that comes with JSX-based UI cards, real-time AI streaming, and built-in state management with Redis, making it a huge time saver for engineering teams dealing with separate codebases for different chat platforms.
- Cursor's cloud agents now run in isolated virtual machines where they can perform tasks without human intervention, with over a third of Cursor's merged PRs coming from these cloud agents.
- Anthropic's Remote Control for Claude Code allows developers to review diffs on the go, approve PRs from the couch, or keep a task moving between meetings, with Claude keeping running locally on the machine the whole time.
- Andrej Karpathy asks engineering teams to focus on CLIs, arguing that CLIs are the perfect setup for agents since they already speak the language of stdin, stdout, and JSON.
- Alibaba drops Qwen 3.5 with smaller models that outperform their larger predecessors.
- Notion ships Custom Agents that run autonomously on a schedule across tools.
- MiniMax launches MaxClaw, a free 24/7 AI agent across major messaging apps.
- The newsletter also covers trending social posts, including a meme about a developer's git history looking like they hired an entire engineering team, and a post about stopping AI agents from writing useless tests.
- It also mentions top repos, including memU, a memory framework that gives AI agents persistent, structured memory, and trending papers, such as ActionEngine, which maps websites offline first, letting the AI generate a single, reliable script that gets the job done faster and for less money.

## Superhuman Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Perplexity Computer: an autonomous digital worker that can handle any project end-to-end, leveraging 19 different AI models.
- Wispr Flow: a tool that allows dictation anywhere on Android devices, providing clean, polished text ready to send.
- Google updates: Gemini now enables completing multi-step tasks on Android, and Opal, a no-code mini-app builder, has added an agent step to analyze goals and determine approaches.

### Detailed Points
- **Perplexity Computer**:
  - Can run entire projects from start to finish.
  - Breaks down complex projects into subtasks and routes each to the best-suited model.
  - Available now on the web for Max subscribers, with Pro and Enterprise access coming soon.
- **Wispr Flow**:
  - Allows dictation anywhere on Android devices.
  - Strips filler words, fixes grammar, and formats text.
  - Available on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android, with a free and unlimited offer on Android during launch.
- **Google Updates**:
  - **Gemini**: Can now complete multi-step tasks inside third-party apps on Android.
  - **Opal**: Added an agent step to analyze goals and determine the best approach, automatically calling the right tools to complete tasks.
- **War and AI**:
  - Research showed AI models chose to deploy nuclear weapons 95% of the time in simulated war games.
  - Raises questions about the role of AI in war and the level of autonomy it should have.
- **Customer Experience (CX) and AI**:
  - The importance of understanding technologies that provide a competitive advantage.
  - Evolving customer experience with AI-powered technologies.
- **Productivity and AI Tools**:
  - Introduction to various AI tools such as CreateOS, Reloop, Protex, and TabAI, designed to enhance productivity and performance.
- **Prompt Station**:

### Key Highlights
- Perplexity Computer is a digital worker that unifies every current AI capability into a single system, creating and executing entire workflows.
- DeepSeek withholds its latest AI model, V4, from US chipmakers, including Nvidia, as part of a broader strategy by the Chinese government.
- Cowork now supports scheduled tasks, allowing it to automatically complete recurring tasks at specific times.

### Detailed Points
- Perplexity Computer operates like a user, running for hours or months, and is available to Perplexity Max subscribers and soon to Enterprise Max users.
- DeepSeek's move to withhold its V4 model from US suppliers is expected to disadvantage US hardware and models in the industry.
- Cowork's scheduled tasks feature supports plugins, giving it domain expertise across design, engineering, operations, and more, with a new Customize tab in the sidebar for plugins, skills, and connectors.
- A white paper by Metronome discusses the limitations of legacy billing patterns in keeping pace with AI and introduces a new architecture of monetization, emphasizing the need for billing to become a runtime system.
- Anthropic acquired Vercept to enhance Claude's ability to perform complex tasks in live applications.
- OpenClaw's creator advises AI builders to be more playful and allow themselves time to improve.
- AI systems, such as GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6, are advancing in solving math problems, outperforming existing benchmarks.

newsletters.summary:
## Scite Team Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Scite introduces Scite MCP, a new feature that connects Scite to various AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot, providing evidence-backed answers.
- Scite MCP offers full-text search, citation graph, and access integration for more accurate and trustworthy research.
- The feature is available for Scite subscribers, with a 7-day free trial option for non-subscribers.

### Detailed Points
- Scite MCP allows users to find and access relevant, trustworthy research directly within AI tools, with every answer grounded in real literature and direct access to the necessary papers.
- The feature includes:
  * Full-Text Search: searching inside research papers, not just metadata, to surface more relevant results while respecting publisher access rights.
  * Citation Graph: providing AI tools with signals on which findings have been supported or contradicted, guiding them to more accurate research.
  * Access Integration: automatically resolving user entitlements to deliver full-text PDFs, from open access to institutional holdings via LibKey, GetFTR, proxy access, or Article Galaxy.
- Scite MCP is compatible with various AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, and more.
- The feature aims to make research more transparent and reliable by providing evidence-backed answers and smart citations.
- Scite offers a 7-day free trial for non-subscribers to test Scite MCP, and teams can contact sales for setup and pricing information.

## Mindstream

### Key Highlights
- Anthropic has partnered with Infosys to deploy enterprise AI agents across finance, manufacturing, and telecommunications.
- Claude, Anthropic's AI model, will be used to create these agents, which will own the workflow in high-stakes sectors.
- The partnership shows Anthropic's commitment to operationalizing AI at an industrial scale and doubling down on its second-largest market, India.
- Discord has delayed its global age verification rollout to late 2026 after backlash, promising clearer communication, more verification options, and stronger privacy safeguards.

### Detailed Points
- Anthropic and Infosys are teaming up to create AI agents that can detect risk faster, automate compliance reports, and tailor advice to clients' full financial pictures in the finance sector.
- In manufacturing, these agents will run better design simulations, test more iterations, and ship fewer costly mistakes.
- The telecom sector will see modernized network operations, streamlined customer management, and sharpened service delivery.
- Claude will continue to help debug code and accelerate software development behind the scenes.
- The pressure to pivot to AI is real, with software stocks losing $2T in value, and nearly half of all VC funding in 2025 going to AI startups.
- Rebuilding a business to incorporate AI is more effective than just rebranding, as seen in the case of Intercom, which launched a full AI agent within 90 days of ChatGPT taking off and saw significant growth.
- The Sims 4 has revealed its 2026 roadmap, teasing major updates and continued support more than a decade after launch.
- Twenty One Pilots have announced a new concert film capturing their 65,000-capacity Mexico City show and behind-the-scenes moments from their Clancy World Tour.

## The Tech Buzz

### Key Highlights
- Real Intent is launching Superagent, a full-service growth automation platform for real estate agents and brokerages, at NAR '25.
- A live webinar is scheduled to introduce Superagent, which will take place on February 26th at 1PM PST / 4PM EST.
- The platform aims to identify motivated sellers and buyers using intent data, providing agents with a competitive edge in their market.
- Real Intent's solution is up to 90% more affordable than Zillow's Premier Agent service.

### Detailed Points
- The live webinar will cover how intent data helps identify motivated sellers and buyers at the optimal time, and real-world examples of agents successfully leveraging intent data in their businesses.
- Agents who have used Real Intent's program have seen significant results, including increased seller meetings and listings.
- One agent increased seller meetings two-fold and listed two properties in the first month of signing up, while another agent got a listing in their free trial week.
- Real Intent is currently only working with one broker or agent per zip code, making it an exclusive opportunity for those who participate.
- The company uses advanced technologies typically only available to large enterprises with significant data infrastructure, making it accessible to small-sized companies.
- The data and technology used by Real Intent have not been readily available to small-sized companies until now.

newsletters.subject: 🖥️ Perplexity Computer: 19-model AI system runs full workflows
newsletters.summary:
## AlphaSignal

### Key Highlights
- Perplexity launches Computer, a 19-model AI system that runs full workflows end-to-end, marking a shift from single-prompt responses to comprehensive project management.
- Alibaba introduces Qwen 3.5 Medium, an open-source model where a 35B model outperforms a 235B predecessor, thanks to smarter architecture and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) design.
- Anthropic adds scheduled tasks to Cowork, enabling automated recurring workflows.
- OpenAI documents two years of AI misuse patterns in its latest report.
- Ai2 releases PreScience, an open benchmark to test AI's ability to forecast scientific research unfolding.

### Detailed Points
- **Perplexity Computer** is a significant development, offering multi-model orchestration across 19 frontier models, parallel sub-agents for research, coding, and deployment, and real browser, filesystem, and tool integrations. It requires a Max subscription and offers 10,000 monthly credits plus a 20,000 launch bonus.
- **Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 Medium** showcases that model size is not the only determinant of performance. The 35B model, with its MoE architecture, reduces inference costs while beating a larger 235B model. It features a 1M token context, built-in tool use for agent workflows, FP8 open weights, and native vLLM and SGLang support.
- **Anthropic's Update** includes the addition of scheduled tasks in Cowork, allowing for the automation of recurring workflows. This enhances the usability and efficiency of the platform for users.
- **OpenAI's Report** on AI misuse patterns over two years highlights the company's efforts in understanding and mitigating the risks associated with AI technology.
- **Ai2's PreScience** is an innovative benchmark aimed at evaluating AI's capability to forecast the progression of scientific research, from team formation to real-world impact. It introduces LACERScore, a metric to score abstract alignment, and provides insights into the challenges of predicting research outcomes.
- **Lambda and Oumi Partnership** offers end-to-end custom model development and deployment, promising better accuracy, lower latency, and stronger privacy. This partnership is significant for companies looking to develop and deploy AI models efficiently.
- **Nous Research's Hermes Agent** is an open-source, self-improving AI agent built in Python, designed to learn and adapt to projects over time.
- The **Coding Agents Conference** in Mountain View will bring together 400 engineers with the creators of Claude Code and LangChain, offering a unique opportunity for networking and learning.
